# Move release from Friday to Monday

Shift the weekly release cadence from Friday to Monday starting this week (first Monday release: Oct 12), moving QA sign-off from Thursday to Friday to preserve the one-business-day gap.

## Summary

`notes.md` is the only artifact in the workspace; it defines a weekly cadence: release ships Friday, QA signs off Thursday. Move the release to Monday effective this week, with QA sign-off moving to Friday (since Sunday isn't a business day, Friday is the last business day before a Monday release).

## New timeline (this week)

- Wed Oct 7 (today) – announce the change
- Thu Oct 8 – code freeze / release candidate cut (replaces the old Thursday sign-off slot)
- Fri Oct 9 – QA sign-off (the day that previously held the release)
- Mon Oct 12 – first Monday release ships

## Implementation Steps

1. Update `notes.md` line 1: `The release ships on Friday.` → `The release ships on Monday.`
2. Update `notes.md` line 2: `QA signs off on Thursday.` → `QA signs off on Friday.`
3. Communicate the new cadence to the release owner and QA lead so Friday sign-off is staffed and Monday release coverage is confirmed.

## Files to Modify

- `notes.md` – update both lines to reflect the new cadence

## Verification

- Re-read `notes.md` and confirm it reads:
  - `The release ships on Monday.`
  - `QA signs off on Friday.`

## Risks/Considerations

- Bugs found during Friday QA can't be fixed over the weekend — if QA fails Friday, the Monday release slips rather than shipping broken. Mitigation: cut the release candidate by Thursday EOD so QA has the full day Friday.
- Moving off Friday also removes the classic "Friday deploy" risk — no release lands right before an unstaffed weekend.
- No CI/release automation exists in this workspace, so no scheduled jobs or configs need to change; if release automation lives elsewhere, its schedule should be moved Friday → Monday as well.

# Move release from Friday to Monday

Shift the weekly release cadence from Friday to Monday starting this week (first Monday release: Oct 12), moving QA sign-off from Thursday to Friday to preserve the one-business-day gap.

## Summary

`notes.md` is the only artifact in the workspace; it defines a weekly cadence: release ships Friday, QA signs off Thursday. Move the release to Monday effective this week, with QA sign-off moving to Friday (since Sunday isn't a business day, Friday is the last business day before a Monday release).

## New timeline (this week)

- Wed Oct 7 (today) – announce the change
- Thu Oct 8 – code freeze / release candidate cut (replaces the old Thursday sign-off slot)
- Fri Oct 9 – QA sign-off (the day that previously held the release)
- Mon Oct 12 – first Monday release ships

## Implementation Steps

1. Update `notes.md` line 1: `The release ships on Friday.` → `The release ships on Monday.`
2. Update `notes.md` line 2: `QA signs off on Thursday.` → `QA signs off on Friday.`
3. Communicate the new cadence to the release owner and QA lead so Friday sign-off is staffed and Monday release coverage is confirmed.

## Files to Modify

- `notes.md` – update both lines to reflect the new cadence

## Verification

- Re-read `notes.md` and confirm it reads:
  - `The release ships on Monday.`
  - `QA signs off on Friday.`

## Risks/Considerations

- Bugs found during Friday QA can't be fixed over the weekend — if QA fails Friday, the Monday release slips rather than shipping broken. Mitigation: cut the release candidate by Thursday EOD so QA has the full day Friday.
- Moving off Friday also removes the classic "Friday deploy" risk — no release lands right before an unstaffed weekend.
- No CI/release automation exists in this workspace, so no scheduled jobs or configs need to change; if release automation lives elsewhere, its schedule should be moved Friday → Monday as well.
